evidence.quote: **Tumbling windows** are windows defined entirely by the time intervals they capture. These time intervals don't overlap.

The TUMBLE function assigns each element to a window of specified
window size. Tumbling windows have a fixed size and do not overlap.

edits.old: Non-overlap describes window membership. It does not establish exactly-once end-to-end delivery, guarantee inclusion of arbitrarily late events, or guarantee an output every interval of wall-clock time. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Tumbling-window intervals don't overlap; that describes window membership. In Atlas Stream Processing, event-time windows close on watermark progress rather than at the wall-clock end of the interval, so output is not guaranteed every wall-clock interval. Documents that arrive after their window has closed are treated as late-arriving and sent to the Dead Letter Queue if one is configured. allowedLateness only delays closing by a set interval, so inclusion of arbitrarily late events is not guaranteed. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/windows.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md
